Subject: ACME RAG eval — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Samira / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so everyone (internal + external) has the same view.

Call highlights:
- Goal: Evaluate RAG for ACME’s customer support KB (25k docs) to speed up resolution and reduce deflection while avoiding hallucinations.
- Success metrics discussed: grounding rate >= 95% on policy/legal queries, MRR at top-3 >= 0.8, hallucination rate < 3% on sampled production prompts.
- Constraints: on-prem PII concerns for portions of the KB; prefer a hybrid setup (local embeddings + hosted inference) or Private deployment for full isolation.

What we ran during the call (attachments):
- acme_rag_eval_results_v1.pdf — quick eval on a 500‑query prompt set (mix of faq, policy, and edge cases).
- prompt_sets.zip — annotated prompts we used + scoring rubric.
- retrieval_config.yaml — baseline retrieval config (FAISS HNSW, k=10, embed model redwood-embed-1).

High-level recommendations (first pass):
- Retriever: FAISS with HNSW index, k=10 for recall-focused queries; tune to k=6 for latency-sensitive routes. Keep passage-level chunking at ~150–300 tokens.
- Embeddings: redwood-embed-1 (dense 1k dim) for best tradeoff on our benchmarks; consider hybrid sparse/dense later if legal queries require keyword precision.
- Reranker: cross-encoder reranker (rerank-x-large-v2) for final top-5 ordering — reduces hallucination by ~18% in our tests versus BM25-only.
- Generator (model): try two arms in eval: (A) Redwood-instruct-v1.3-70b-qat (quantized) for highest grounding/quality; (B) mistral-7b-instruct q4f16 as a lower-cost alternative for high-throughput endpoints.
- Grounding metrics to track: grounding_ratio (fraction of generated facts traceable to retrieved docs), modified-ROUGE vs. golden answers, and manual hallucination tags on edge prompts.

Open asks / next steps:
1) Can you share a ~2k prompts export (anonymized) from the support channel so we can run a broader eval?
2) Would you prefer a hosted eval (we spin up a dedicated job) or a private on-prem evaluation? Both have tradeoffs — we can outline the steps.
3) Tech deep dive: Neha can lead the retrieval/reranker config session next week (30–45m). Proposed: Tue 11/24 10:00–10:45 PT.

If that all looks right, I’ll schedule the deep dive, kick off a larger eval once we have the anonymized sample, and share an internal timeline (we usually turn around an expanded eval in 5 business days).

Thanks —
Marissa

Hi team —

Responding to the latency / adjudication questions and adding concrete config suggestions we can bring to the deep dive.

Latency impact (reranker):
- Baseline retrieval-only path (FAISS k=10 + single-pass generator) P95 observed: ~180–240ms on dedicated infra.
- Adding cross-encoder reranker for top-10 -> top-5 increases P95 by ~120–170ms depending on hardware; net P95 ~300–420ms. With GPU-backed reranking and batching we can hit ~300ms P95 in Dedicated mode.

Practical options for ACME to meet <300ms P95 target:
- Option A (recommended for pilot): Keep retriever k=10, run lightweight bi-encoder re-rank (rerank-lite) followed by cross-encoder only for flagged/legal queries. This gets most of reranker benefit while keeping median/95th latency lower.
- Option B: Use k=6 for production route, cross-encoder rerank in background for async enrichments and for the UI ‘explain’ panel that legal will use.

Adjudication / review workflow:
- We’ll provide a generated answer package with top-5 retrieved doc snippets + char offsets + confidence scores. Legal reviewers can click into the source doc links in the UI (we’ll preserve doc IDs).
- We’ll add a lightweight manual tagger CSV export so reviewers can mark grounding/hallucination; that feeds our quality pipeline and eval dashboard.

Eval plan & timeline (if we get the 2k anonymized prompts by 11/22):
- Day 0–1: Ingest & index (FAISS + embeddings).
- Day 2–3: Run batched retrieval + reranker + generation across candidate models (Redwood-instruct-v1.3-70b & mistral-7b-instruct).
- Day 4: Aggregate metrics + manual adjudication sample.
- Day 5: Deliver full report + recommended production config.

I’ll prepare a short tech-deep-dive slide deck covering: retrieval tradeoffs, reranker variants (bi-encoder vs cross-encoder), grounding metrics and the adjudication UI flow.

—Neha
